Love E.A.S.Y. I'm amused by the negative reviewers who state that the author promotes a one-way-for-all method.  We followed the advice given in this book 15 years ago. It was wonderful.  I breastfed for 9 months with plenty of milk and my son thrived on a schedule. Now, this doesn't mean you have to follow a strict schedule; modify it to your needs. I fed on demand and we were cosleeping  for about 3 weeks. My husband and I took turns in separate bedrooms and he would bring our son to me when time to feed during the night. I didn't start this method until he was about 9 weeks, then slowly integrated the steps. I still kept 1-2 night feedings (he wasn't "awake" but would latch on perfectly),then slowly weaned from those.  Since I had to go back to work after 10 weeks, he was sleeping 6-7 hours every night, I breastfed every morning, pumped everyday for daily feeding(s) with home childcare service, 2-3 more feedings before bed 7-8pm.  He also took a naps about the same times everyday and all of us were sooo happy!  We were very active AND enjoyed "scheduling" around him.  He was (and still is) trending on target for all milestones! To this day he is a wonderful sleeper, healthy, active and smart.  Take TIME to integrate if needed, but a schedule is the way for ALL to enjoy the fantastic lives of parents. Look, evidence-based research says stress and lack of sleep for moms is more harmful than scheduling baby time.  Once again, you do not have to start abruptly.

Amelia Bedelia Digs In Geared towards 7-8-year-olds, a bit of this content will go over their heads, told in a voice that seems older than its main character and its intended audience. This may not work for all children.

Summer is another time for another adventure for Amelia Bedelia. Summer vacation means time spent at her family’s beach house with her Mom, Dad, dog Finally and her best friend from camp, Alice—along with extended family.

Summertime fun is not the only thing that occupies Amelia’s time. Her time is also spent discovering surfing and finding out pirates once lived on the island she’s now staying on.

The story was youthful, filled with giggles, silly jokes, and kid-like adventure. As mentioned some of the lingo, and scenes felt a little old for a book intended for kids under 10.

There’s mention of romance and idioms that I don’t think a child will understand. I don’t believe it will deter the enjoyment of the novel, it's not quite as child-like as anticipated.

Caricatures and fun drawings do bring this story to life and give it a journal-like feel.

At under 200 pages, with wide spaces and clear-to-read font, it shouldn’t be too long of a read for young children reading at chapter book level.

A decent read, with some issues, but should be an enjoyable read for kids with big summer dreams and a wild imagination.

Better than expected I must not have been paying very close attention when I first grabbed this book, as I thought it was a novel. I am very glad I got a copy of it though. This book really spoke to me. I've never really known if I wanted to get married or not. The idea always seemed very romantic and lovely but when you are actually in a relationship with someone, the reality of wants and needs is a stark contrast to the ideal. I've always been such an introvert and value my alone time to such a degree that I'm pretty sure that I won't ever meet anyone that I enjoy spending the majority of my time with more than being alone. This is something that most people, and society in general, don't understand could possibly be desirable for a woman. This book is a ray of hope that it might someday be not so strange and a reminder that many women have been quite happy on their own for many, many years. Women do not need to "consider the love of a man the most supreme of all social validations" and society doesn't need to believe that she should.

5 stars! Many years ago I picked up Kiss an Angel to read. I had never read a book by Susan Elizabeth Phillips but the premise this book was based on was intriguing. Best one in this series! WOW! Seldom does a romance novel contain so much excitement, drama and sweet romance that I spend hours on this kind of emotional rollercoaster. Fashion has always been Riley's dream but she couldn't seem to get ahead in the field. They say it's all about who you know so when Riley's portfolio finds it's way into Josh's hands it isn't long before Riley has moved to NY with the hopes of seeing her dreams finally come true.

But as in many cut-throat businesses there will always be someone willing to cross the line to get ahead. Josh and Riley's sweet relationship is barely getting started when their love will be put to the test and Riley's very honor will be called into question, while Josh will have to make the most difficult decision he has ever been faced with.

The story focuses on Georgia transplants Shannon Mackenna, her 5 year old daughter Kayleigh, and Shannon's grandmother Gracie. This small but tightknit family find themselves a part of the Tampa Suns world as Shannon's gym becomes a place some of them workout in during off hours. When Shannon comes face to face with a part of her past, Cam, she knows her world is going to change. She keeps Cam at bay, but that can only last for so long.

This is a great second chance love story where they both find they are enfolded into each others world. Cam fights hard to win Shannon over, and it seems she's inspired a very chivalrous side to him. Their influence in each other is organic and they truly seem to find in each other a place where they can each be at piece. For Cam, what he finds is that this insta-family is everything he needs, and it's endearing to see the impact Kayleigh has on him. Ryan captures Kayleigh's talk perfectly and I couldn't help but imagine this darling girl.

You HAVE to meet Officer Sexy, Grant Malone! I am speechless and crying after finishing the book! I really enjoyed Cuffed and its also my first book to read by K. Bromberg. I can't wait to see what Bromberg has in store for the other Malone brothers!

First off, you HAVE to meet Officer Sexy, Grant Malone! One of the three Malone boys that all have devoted their lives to saving others. Grant Malone is best childhood friends with Emerson Reeves. Emerson experiences a major trauma at 9 years old and Grant is involved with breaking their pinky promise over a shared secret.

"Head up. Wings out."

The book is packed with witty banter, a cat and mouse game, and of course Officer Sexy! If you are a fan of K. Bromberg then I am sure you will love Cuffed and if you enjoy a childhood friends to lovers book then this is definitely for you! "I've only ever loved two men.
Both were taken away in handcuffs.
One because he hurt me.
The other because he tried to save her.
And in the end, save me."

Play Ball! Only seventeen, Kat Miller joins the new women’s professional softball league to play the summer before her senior year. A skilled player, she has some trouble relating to the other players who are mostly older and more worldly wise. She tries to live by her Christian upbringing and maintain her integrity despite the challenges she faces as they practice and play day after day. In addition, a pesky reporter, Jack Raymond, has zeroed in on her as the player to feature, creating more conflict in her life. Kat seems pretty mature for her age, but I think it’s realistic for the time. It was interesting to learn what the female players faced during that time. The story felt true to life and history. This is quite different than the author’s suspense novels I have enjoyed. Her writing skill spreads to other genres as well. You can tell she’s done her research to craft a winning tale. I received a copy from Celebrate Lit. All opinions are my own.

SciFi Drivel Earthfall, Book I Black Sand, has a subpar storyline, populated by a cast of one dimensional, lackluster characters (excepting the narrating main character-who is both annoying and buffoonish), immature and pretentious writing and mediocre editing.

At 10% (cannot tell you exact page, as this is another eBook devoid of pages, only location-geez!) into the book, I was ready to put it down, believing the eBook author to be a juvenile, writing for juveniles-shame on me. I checked the author's bio and discovered the immature writing was not caused by the author's chronological age.

What is the author's obsession with Carl Sagan, video games, pop culture and movies of the 1980's and 1990's? It does not add to the book; it distracts and detracts, making the reader wonder if the author has some form of middle age crisis.

awesome! This was one of those books that I picked at random, not expecting much. I was wrong. I literally found myself nervously chewing my lip, and realized I had my "freaked out" eyebrows on, multiple times. You know a book is good when you start making faces while reading!! Ruger and Chastity 3.5 stars

Off Limits is book 5 in the Kings of Mayhem series and although I haven't read any other books in this series I felt it read fine as a standalone. Now if you follow my reviews you know I love books with an age gap, add in some bikers and I'm sold. Overall it was a pretty good story but I did have some issues. My main issue was that the author did to much telling and I had a hard time connecting to the couple in the beginning. They seemed to be doing their own thing and then boom their in love. After all, Reed (along with John Cale) made a memorial album for Warhol after his death, I figured there had to be some close connection.
I was disappointed on both points. Well, I did learn a lot about Warhol and the people around him, but it seemed mostly superficial. I don't understand him any better, and I never got a strong impression that the author understood him either.
On the positive side, the book contains a wealth of information about the New York art scene in the fifties and sixties. This would be a great book for an art history class, with its many references to people and places.
On the other hand, Warhol's homosexuality seemed to be the true emphasis of the book, with almost every reference to Warhol or his art pointing out how gay he or his art was. That seemed to be the primary interest the author had in Warhol, rather than his art.
For me the book seemed way too long. Too much trivia was included. Maybe a good edit would have helped.

A Delightful Series Conclusion Welp. The Maddening Lord Montwood was great. I was anxious to begin Lucan's book because he was the last rake standing in the wager that began the series, but also nervous because I was afraid once I got to know Lucan, I would not like him. I was worried that "maddening" meant Lucan's darkness would cause him to be cruel, wish-washy with Frances's heart. That he would want her one minute, only to push her away the next. Thankfully, Lord Montwood is "maddening" because of how quickly he pulled France's's heart to his. He was so easily and thoroughly likable, lovable actually. Lucan was my favorite kind of hero: quietly honorable, kind, a devoted friend, and once he falls in love, he is absolutely done for.

Frances Thorne was a wonderfully written match for Lucan. She was a smart heroine, one who devoted her time to empowering herself and other women, especially those easily taken advantage of. She also was a determined woman who knew her heart well enough to know that she could never fight love. These two absolutely knew they were in love with each other, and there was no second guessing. That was refreshing.

The Maddening Lord had an interesting plot, full of turns and devious complications. I was thoroughly engaged, and enjoyed the fact that I couldn't see the exact resolutions coming down the way. Using religious ideas and putting them into a real world solution for a better life, you will find that spirituality doesn’t have to hit you over the head and knock you out. I loved how personal this book was, and how easy it was to read. Not only that, I enjoyed the religious tones and more importantly, the larger picture.

The explanations of the inner patterns really found its way into my perception. Not only that, in chapter six, the notion of fixing instinct was definitely well rooted in a good thing. The story itself is quite cliche and predictable. What do you think will happen in a horror story called "The Doll"? Well, that's exactly what happens. EXACTLY.

The writing is competent, though occasionally awkward. When the heroes first meet the doll, the book describes it as "Chucky-like," which is a fairly egregious use of imagery to invoke one famous scary doll to describe another scary doll.

Still, though the story is predictable, it goes through the motions in a relatively solid way, conjuring up a few decent scares throughout. The details about the Santeria religion/magic are by far the book's best moments, borrowing from actual occult darkness to lend credibility to its own story.

Ravenous fans of the horror genre might enjoy this book moreso than casual fans that are familiar with the usual Twilight Zone-style twists and rhythm to a story like this.

I'll plug Mike Miller's "Kill Thy Neighbor" again - an amazing and unique story that's incredibly intense, interesting and different than 99% of the short stories out there.

ISIS (the Taliban and Al Qaeda) differ markedly from the organizations with which I'm familiar in terms of composition and objectives. Lily’s message is unique in that it is not a written message but a drawing, since she is an artist. Josh, who has the drawing, did not find the bottle but bought the drawing on eBay. His motive in reaching out to Lily was only to get a revised version of the drawing to use in advertising. And there begins the story. I dislike reviews that give too many details, because the reader should discover those details for him/herself. Therefore, I shall only comment that the author describes emotions and scenery so well that the reader lives vicariously in the lives of Lily and Josh. Not only does Ms. Knight tell a good story, she offers some sage advice on relationships, especially on releasing oneself from the emotional bonds of a previous abusive relationship. Lily’s story is an excellent short-ish feel-good story. I recommend it for a beach read or while curled up in a comfy chair on a rainy afternoon.
